answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring every new identity to lock a refundable bond and earn reputation through signed, useful transactions with established peers. Random challenge tasks and cross-checks expose clones that coordinate or fabricate work; proven fraud slashes the bond and lowers connected reputations. Creating hundreds of fake agents therefore demands separate capital and sustained activity, while collusion risks forfeiture. Even at the wharf, a nadir in trust costs more than a quill can cheaply conceal.
